### graze.share_links.DROPBOX_PATH_KINDS *= (('/scl/fi/', ShareLinkKind.FILE), ('/scl/fo/', ShareLinkKind.ARCHIVE), ('/s/', ShareLinkKind.FILE), ('/sh/', ShareLinkKind.ARCHIVE))*

Share-link path prefixes -> what they denote. `/s/` + `/sh/` are the legacy
forms; `/scl/fi/` + `/scl/fo/` are the ones Dropbox issues today.

### graze.share_links.PASSTHROUGH_SCHEMES *= ('http', 'https')*

this module
describes *fetchable web resources*, and unknown schemes are not that.

* **Type:**
  Schemes a plain URL may pass through with. Anything else is refused

### *class* graze.share_links.ResolvedShareLink(url, provider, kind, direct_url=None, reason=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

What a share URL denotes, and how (or whether) to fetch it.

* **Parameters:**
  * **url** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The share URL as given (stripped of surrounding whitespace).
  * **provider** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Provider slug, e.g. `'dropbox'`, `'google_drive'`,
    `'onedrive'`, `'http'` (a plain URL that is nobody’s share link),
    or `'unknown'`.
  * **kind** ([`ShareLinkKind`](_autosummary/graze.share_links.html.md#graze.share_links.ShareLinkKind)) – See [`ShareLinkKind`](_autosummary/graze.share_links.html.md#graze.share_links.ShareLinkKind).
  * **direct_url** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – A URL whose response body is the content – or `None` when
    the link cannot be resolved without a provider API.
  * **reason** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – Why `direct_url` is `None`. Required whenever it is.

`direct_url` and `kind` are independent: a Google Workspace document is a
`FILE` that still has no resolvable download URL.

```pycon
>>> r = ResolvedShareLink('https://x/y', 'http', ShareLinkKind.FILE, 'https://x/y')
>>> r.resolved
True
```

An unresolved link must say why – an adapter that refuses silently is a bug:

```pycon
>>> ResolvedShareLink('https://x/y', 'nope', ShareLinkKind.UNKNOWN)
Traceback (most recent call last):
    ...
ValueError: An unresolved ResolvedShareLink must carry a reason (url: https://x/y)
```

#### *property* resolved *: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*

True when there is a direct URL to fetch.

### *class* graze.share_links.ShareLinkKind(\*values)

Bases: [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Enum`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/enum.html#enum.Enum)

What a share link denotes – a file, an archive, a folder, or unknown.

`ARCHIVE` is a refinement of `FILE`: the URL still resolves to one blob,
but that blob is a ZIP the caller must expand into N assets. Providers render
*folder* links this way (Dropbox does so even for a single-file folder).

`FOLDER` is the honest answer when a link denotes a folder and the provider
offers **no** URL that downloads it – listing it needs an API credential.

```pycon
>>> ShareLinkKind.ARCHIVE.value
'archive'
>>> ShareLinkKind('folder') is ShareLinkKind.FOLDER
True
```

### *exception* graze.share_links.ShareLinkResolutionError

Bases: [`ValueError`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError)

Raised when a share link cannot be resolved to a direct-download URL.

### graze.share_links.ShareLinkResolver

given a URL, return its resolution, or `None` for “not mine”.

* **Type:**
  An adapter

alias of `Callable`[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`ResolvedShareLink`](_autosummary/graze.share_links.html.md#graze.share_links.ResolvedShareLink) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]

### graze.share_links.add_share_link_resolver(provider, resolver)

Register (or replace) a provider adapter.

`resolver` takes a URL and returns a [`ResolvedShareLink`](_autosummary/graze.share_links.html.md#graze.share_links.ResolvedShareLink), or `None`
to mean “not mine, try the next one”. Replacing an existing provider keeps its
position in the try-order; a new one is appended (so it is tried last).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### graze.share_links.direct_download_url(url, , resolvers=None)

The URL to actually fetch, or raise [`ShareLinkResolutionError`](_autosummary/graze.share_links.html.md#graze.share_links.ShareLinkResolutionError).

```pycon
>>> direct_download_url('https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AbC/view')
'https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1AbC'
>>> direct_download_url('https://1drv.ms/u/s!AbCd')
Traceback (most recent call last):
    ...
graze.share_links.ShareLinkResolutionError: Cannot resolve this onedrive link...
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### graze.share_links.resolve_dropbox(url)

Resolve a Dropbox share link by forcing `dl=1`.

Both the modern `/scl/` forms and the legacy `/s/` + `/sh/` forms; every
other query parameter (notably `rlkey`, which is a bearer secret) is kept
byte-for-byte.

```pycon
>>> r = resolve_dropbox('https://www.dropbox.com/s/a1/data.csv?dl=0')
>>> r.kind.value, r.direct_url
('file', 'https://www.dropbox.com/s/a1/data.csv?dl=1')
```

A folder link is an *archive* – one ZIP holding N members:

```pycon
>>> r = resolve_dropbox('https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fo/q7/z?rlkey=abc&st=t1')
>>> r.kind.value, r.direct_url
('archive', 'https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fo/q7/z?rlkey=abc&st=t1&dl=1')
```

Non-share Dropbox URLs are not this adapter’s business:

```pycon
>>> resolve_dropbox('https://www.dropbox.com/home') is None
True
>>> resolve_dropbox('https://example.com/s/a1/data.csv?dl=0') is None
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`ResolvedShareLink`](_autosummary/graze.share_links.html.md#graze.share_links.ResolvedShareLink)]

### graze.share_links.resolve_google_drive(url)

Resolve a Google Drive / Google Workspace URL.

Files resolve; **folders and Workspace documents are refused**, because
neither has a plain-URL download and pretending otherwise is how a folder id
ends up in a file-download URL.

```pycon
>>> resolve_google_drive('https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AbC/view').direct_url
'https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1AbC'
```

A `resourcekey` (required by link-shared files created before 2021) is kept:

```pycon
>>> r = resolve_google_drive('https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AbC/view?resourcekey=0-x')
>>> r.direct_url
'https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1AbC&resourcekey=0-x'
```

A folder is a folder – refused, with the reason and the id to hand:

```pycon
>>> r = resolve_google_drive('https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1FoLd')
>>> r.kind.value, r.direct_url is None
('folder', True)
>>> print(r.reason)
Google Drive folder links have no direct-download URL...
```

So is a native Google doc – a file, but not a downloadable one:

```pycon
>>> r = resolve_google_drive('https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Sh/edit')
>>> r.kind.value, r.direct_url is None
('file', True)
```

…\*unless\* the caller already chose a format, which is the only thing the
refusal above was ever about:

```pycon
>>> u = 'https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Sh/export?format=csv&gid=0'
>>> resolve_google_drive(u).direct_url == u
True
```

```pycon
>>> resolve_google_drive('https://example.com/file/d/1AbC/view') is None
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`ResolvedShareLink`](_autosummary/graze.share_links.html.md#graze.share_links.ResolvedShareLink)]

### graze.share_links.resolve_onedrive(url)

Recognise a OneDrive / SharePoint share link, and refuse it.

```pycon
>>> r = resolve_onedrive('https://1drv.ms/f/s!AbCd')
>>> r.provider, r.kind.value, r.direct_url is None
('onedrive', 'folder', True)
```

```pycon
>>> r = resolve_onedrive('https://contoso-my.sharepoint.com/:v:/g/personal/x/EaB')
>>> r.provider, r.kind.value
('onedrive', 'unknown')
```

An ordinary SharePoint document path is not a share link:

```pycon
>>> resolve_onedrive('https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/x/clip.mp4') is None
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`ResolvedShareLink`](_autosummary/graze.share_links.html.md#graze.share_links.ResolvedShareLink)]

### graze.share_links.resolve_share_url(url, , resolvers=None)

Describe what a share URL denotes and how (or whether) to fetch it.

* **Parameters:**
  * **url** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The URL as a user pasted it. Surrounding whitespace is stripped.
  * **resolvers** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`ResolvedShareLink`](_autosummary/graze.share_links.html.md#graze.share_links.ResolvedShareLink)]]]]) – Adapters to try, in order. Defaults to
    [`share_link_resolvers`](_autosummary/graze.share_links.html.md#graze.share_links.share_link_resolvers); pass your own to test in isolation.
* **Return type:**
  [`ResolvedShareLink`](_autosummary/graze.share_links.html.md#graze.share_links.ResolvedShareLink)
* **Returns:**
  A [`ResolvedShareLink`](_autosummary/graze.share_links.html.md#graze.share_links.ResolvedShareLink). Never raises for an unresolvable link –
  the refusal is in the return value (`direct_url is None` plus a
  `reason`). Use [`direct_download_url()`](_autosummary/graze.share_links.html.md#graze.share_links.direct_download_url) when you want the raise.

```pycon
>>> resolve_share_url('  https://www.dropbox.com/s/a1/x.csv?dl=0  ').direct_url
'https://www.dropbox.com/s/a1/x.csv?dl=1'
>>> resolve_share_url('https://example.com/a.mp4').provider
'http'
>>> resolve_share_url('ftp://example.com/a.mp4').resolved
False
```

### graze.share_links.share_link_resolvers *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [Optional](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[ResolvedShareLink](_autosummary/graze.share_links.html.md#graze.share_links.ResolvedShareLink)]]]* *= {'dropbox': <function resolve_dropbox>, 'google_drive': <function resolve_google_drive>, 'onedrive': <function resolve_onedrive>}*

Provider adapters, tried in order; the first non-`None` result wins. Open-closed:
extend it with [`add_share_link_resolver()`](_autosummary/graze.share_links.html.md#graze.share_links.add_share_link_resolver) instead of editing this module.

### graze.util.clog(condition, \*args, log_func=<built-in function print>, \*\*kwargs)

Conditional log

```pycon
>>> clog(False, "logging this")
>>> clog(True, "logging this")
logging this
```

One common usage is when there’s a verbose flag that allows the user to specify
whether they want to log or not. Instead of having to litter your code with
`if verbose:` statements you can just do this:

```pycon
>>> verbose = True  # say versbose is True
>>> _clog = clog(verbose)  # makes a clog with a fixed condition
>>> _clog("logging this")
logging this
```

You can also choose a different log function:

```pycon
>>> _clog = clog(True, log_func=lambda x: print(f"hello {x}"))
>>> _clog("logging this")
hello logging this
```

### graze.util.download_from_google_drive(url, file=None, , chk_size=1024, user_agent='Wget/1.16 (linux-gnu)', skip_virus_scan_confirmation_page=False)

Download a file from a Google Drive URL.
Will write the downloaded contents bytes to `file`, which can be a local file path
or file-like object.
If `file=None`, returns the bytes of the contents of the url.

Only FILE urls (`...drive.google.com/file/d/{file_id}...`, `/open?id=`, and the
already-direct `/uc?...id=` and `drive.usercontent.google.com/download?id=` forms)
can be downloaded. A *folder* url, or a Google Workspace document (docs, sheets,
slides, forms), raises `ShareLinkResolutionError` – see
`google_drive_download_url`.

### graze.util.download_from_share_link(url, file=None, , chk_size=1024, user_agent='Wget/1.16 (linux-gnu)')

Resolve a share link to its direct-download URL, then download that.

Raises `ShareLinkResolutionError` (a `ValueError`) when the link cannot be
resolved without a provider API – deliberately, in preference to fetching the
share URL itself and silently storing an HTML preview page as if it were the
asset.

Note that what comes back may be an *archive*: a Dropbox folder link downloads
as a single ZIP holding every member. Check
`resolve_share_url(url).kind == ShareLinkKind.ARCHIVE` and expand it (e.g. with
`dol.FilesOfZip`) rather than treating those bytes as one asset.

### graze.util.download_from_special_url(url, file=None, chk_size=1024, user_agent='Wget/1.16 (linux-gnu)')

Download a url’s contents, using a special url route.

### graze.util.download_url_contents(url, file=None, , chk_size=1024, user_agent='Wget/1.16 (linux-gnu)')

Download url contents into a `file` object, or return bytes if `file` is None.

### graze.util.get_content_size(url, , default=None)

Get the content size of a url, if available, without downloading the content.

### graze.util.google_drive_download_url(url)

Get the direct-download url of a Google Drive FILE url.

Raises `ShareLinkResolutionError` for a *folder* URL (enumerating one needs the
Drive API) and for a Google Workspace document (those must be exported, and the
format is a caller decision) – rather than build a file-download URL out of a
folder id, which is what graze used to do.

```pycon
>>> google_drive_download_url('https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Ab/view')
'https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1Ab'
```

### graze.util.human_readable_bytes(num_of_bytes, , approx_marker='~', n_digits=4, base=1000, units=('B', 'KB', 'MB', 'GB', 'TB', 'PB'))

Convert a number of bytes into a human-readable format with units.

* **Parameters:**
  * **num_of_bytes** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – The number of bytes.
  * **approx_marker** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) *,* *optional*) – Marker indicating approximation. Defaults to “~”.
  * **n_digits** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) *,* *optional*) – Number of significant digits in the output. Defaults to 4.
  * **base** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) *,* *optional*) – Conversion base, 1024 or 1000. Defaults to 1000.
  * **units** ([*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple) *,* *optional*) – Units for conversion. Defaults to (‘B’, ‘KB’, ‘MB’, ‘GB’, ‘TB’, ‘PB’).
* **Returns:**
  Human-readable string representing the number of bytes.
* **Return type:**
  [*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### Examples

```pycon
>>> human_readable_bytes(123456)
'~123.456KB'
>>> human_readable_bytes(123456789)
'~123.457MB'
```

Using `base=1000` (default) is the International System of Units (SI) standard.
But base=1024 is a common practice in computing.

```pycon
>>> human_readable_bytes(123456789, base=1024)
'~117.738MB'
```

```pycon
>>> human_readable_bytes(1234567890123)
'~1.235TB'
```

#### TIP
Use `functools.partial` to customize the function to your needs.

```pycon
>>> from functools import partial
>>> readable = partial(
...     human_readable_bytes,
...     approx_marker='approximately ',
...     units=(' bytes', ' kilobytes')
... )
>>> readable(123456)
'approximately 123.456 kilobytes'
```

Note how the function starts using the scientific notation when it runs out of
units.

```pycon
>>> readable(123456789)
'approximately 1.235e+08 kilobytes'
```
